factualPersistence.row: {fact:'INTERRUPTION_DECLARED', eventId, eventKind, athleteId, declaredAt (the review clock), interruption (as sent), inputHash = hash(interruption), provenance.firstRecordedAt}; recorded once per stating report.
factualPersistence.recordedOn: the decision path whatever it decides (also UNSUPPORTED counterfactual failures and a malformed-facts HOLD after the record is built) and every clinical or question early return. Probed: clinical flag, unknown and stale eligibility, standing clinical route, generic RECOVERED, post-race eligibility check (each 1 row, and the next plain weekly review applies it after clearance where clinical).
factualPersistence.malformedFacts: 6 malformations of execution facts (sets not a list, null exercise, string load, null actual, null observation, string response) x 2 carriers: never refused; the break is recorded in 12/12.
factualPersistence.integrityRefusals: Not recorded on the integrity refusals (by design; review request: 'Not on integrity refusals'). Probed 6: tampered reference state, chronology, unknown kind, observations or choices not a list, invalid athlete model; by reading also ledger / loadConfirmations not a list, invalid program, missing authority. The next plain review is then VALID with the silence ceiling re-plan and no return. INTERFACE-3 section 1 and PREREG-3 Delta 1 say a break survives HOLD with no carve-out (QE-R7D-P31-02); the R7D-CASE-1 client and checker cannot produce these reviews.
factualPersistence.appendOnly: Every carried row survives with its facts unchanged (4-step sequence; P10 on all corpora). Not positional: declared rows are emitted after newer execution rows, and the binding context of rows in a return week is re-derived (pre-existing; identical on R7D-FREEZE-1 when the break is stated directly) (QE-R7D-P31-09).
factualPersistence.integrityFilter: Another athlete's row, a row with no hash and a row declared after the decision clock are carried and not read. A row whose facts were changed is not read (test), but the directed tamper case is not a witness of the hash check: with the check removed the tampered days contradict the dates and the return asks anyway (QM31-11 survives the suite). The candidate's hash check does work: a row whose free text was edited after recording, with consistent facts, is not read on the candidate and is read (REESTABLISH) on the QM31-11 mutant (probe appendOnly.rows.tamperedConsistentFacts). A forged row with a recomputed hash is read (the hash is a consistency check, not authentication; same trust model as execution rows) (QE-R7D-P31-12).
factualPersistence.separationFromExecution: Normalization, binding, learning and historicalStateOf never read the rows. Removing either filter (QM31-08, QM31-09) changes no decision: normalization excludes such rows anyway (defence in depth).

evidence: A kept break is applied once and is never read again after the return decided at or after it (T5; author mutant P31-M5 and QM31-06 killed by the directed file).

After a clinical flag, an eligibility question, a standing clinical route or RECOVERED, the first plain review after clearance re-enters from the kept break (REESTABLISH, VALID), never the pre-break plan.
Differential attribution: on all 141 cases the candidate equals R7D-FREEZE-1 with the kept break restated.
The only path back to the pre-break (silence) plan after a stated break is an integrity refusal of the stating review (QE-R7D-P31-02).
A break with a clinical reason stays CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED at every later decision (QE-R7D-P31-01): no resurrection, but no exit.
A break already applied and re-stated with a new event id is applied again (QE-R7D-P31-03): a re-anchored re-entry, not the stale plan.

eventSeparation.evidence: 12 non-return kinds as carriers (directed T1/T4: schedule, systemic and local fatigue, missed session, goal, equipment, event date; probe: unavailable day, nonclinical exercise substitution, progression too easy, double conflict, overperformance): the carrier asks (interruption.reportedOnItsOwn) and adds only REPLAN_FROM_EVIDENCE; the applying return adds only REESTABLISH; nothing of the carrier is applied. A weekly review with block choices asks (choices) and adds nothing; the next plain review applies the break. T7: none of the 19 kinds is VALID before the return.

evidence: Exact replay (same id, same facts): no new row, same decision (T5).
Replay of the declaring carrier after its return: HOLD (reference-state clock), no row, no plan change.
Newer declaration replaces an older unapplied one, also with other dates (T6; P31-M6 killed). Two declarations at the same instant: the later row in the record wins (deterministic by record order).
Correction of an applied kept break by episodeId = the report that first stated it: SAME_BREAK / EXPLICIT / revision 2, history append-only (T6).
Residual: same event id with other break facts on a carrier is neither recorded nor refused; the first row stands and is applied (QE-R7D-P31-10).
Residual: a partial newer declaration (only reason, or only episodeId) replaces a complete kept break, also a clinical-reason one; decisions become ASK (QE-R7D-P31-11).
Residual: an applied break re-stated with a new id is re-applied as SAME_BREAK/DUPLICATE revision 2 (QE-R7D-P31-03).

propertyAndOracle.P17: Sound as coded for (a) and (c). On the dev cases it detects the author's M1 to M4. Gaps: (c) exempts weekly and return reports that do not apply the break; no check that a kept break is applied only once (P31-M5 undetected on DEV-17 to DEV-21; caught only by T5); 'survives HOLD' has no integrity carve-out (QE-R7D-P31-02).
propertyAndOracle.RESTATE_DECLARED_BREAK: Sound: base and restated runs compared on validity, question, pending state, whole plan and phases. Detects M1 to M4. Does not detect M6 (newer declaration ignored) unless a case holds two unapplied declarations, which Delta 6 does not require; does not detect QM31-02 or QM31-04 (no case declares a break with unknown eligibility or during a standing clinical route).
propertyAndOracle.P03_P10: Fire on a forged row (P03), rewritten facts (P03 + P10), a clock rewritten later (P10) and a dropped row (P10; also catches QM31-07 on DEV-19). Do not fire on a wrong clock or athlete at the row's first recording: P03 checks only event id and interruption (QE-R7D-P31-06); the behavioural effect is caught by P17.

securityRouting.answer: YES, route to Security (privacy owner) as a data-minimization and retention item; not a blocker for this synthetic shadow phase.
securityRouting.why: Before Phase 3.1 the free-text reason of a break was never persisted: the program keeps only hash(interruption) and the screen's matched tokens. Now the whole interruption object, including free text, is kept in the completed-work record for the life of the program and travels with every later decision. Probe freeTextReason: a marker string is in the record and in no program, decision output or reference state, on both the carrier path and the weekly-review path. A break's reason is often health information (flu, ankle sprain), sensitive personal data. No new recipient, but longer retention and replication.
optionsForTheOwner: keep reasonCategory, nonclinical, clinicalReason and the screen outcome instead of the text (the F08 re-screen needs the outcome, not the text)
bound the retention (drop the text once a return is applied or a newer declaration replaces it)
accept it with a consumer-side retention rule
securityRouting.alsoNote: The record is consumer-carried and its hash is not authentication: a forged row with a recomputed hash is read (QE-R7D-P31-12).

findings.origin: new: consequence of D1-D3 with F08 open (disclosed in PREREG-3 residuals and INTERFACE-3)
findings.finding: A break whose own reason is clinical is an absorbing state. After qualified clearance every later decision of every kind stays CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED for the rest of the program, whatever training is reported. No truthful conforming input leaves it: a return report with no break, the same break with nonclinical:true and clinicalReason:false, RECOVERED and weekly reviews all stay CLINICAL. Only a newer, different nonclinical declaration leaves it. A partial one (only episodeId) also replaces it, then asks. Fails closed (no dose); not a blocker; must be decided before any consumer use of the kept-break rule.
findings.reproduction: probes/qe31-persistence.mjs scenario clinicalReasonLiveness: RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE week 5 with {reasonCategory:'ILLNESS', reason:'flu', 2 days}; then, after clearance, weekly reviews in weeks 5 to 9 with the plan's sessions reported, all CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED; in week 10, a return with no break, the same break with nonclinical flags and RECOVERED all stay CLINICAL; {episodeId} only gives ASK; a new 1-day WORK break gives REESTABLISH VALID.

findings.finding: INTERFACE-3 section 1 ('a refusal (HOLD)') and PREREG-3 Delta 1 ('sobrevive a ASK, HOLD e CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED') promise retention through HOLD. The runtime deliberately records nothing on integrity and contract refusals: the next plain review is VALID with no return. P17 has no carve-out, so such a case would score a SAFETY_BLOCKER. The R7D-CASE-1 client and checker cannot produce these reviews (they build the contract and lists, and reject unknown kinds), so no holdout case is expected to show it. Malformed execution facts do not refuse. The freeze record's rule text has the same omission.
findings.reproduction: probes/qe31-persistence.mjs scenario earlyReturns: referenceTampered, chronology, unknownKind, observationsNotList, choicesNotList, athleteModelInvalid; each HOLD, 0 rows kept; next plain weekly REPLAN_FROM_EVIDENCE VALID (lostAndStaleValid true).

findings.origin: pre-existing semantics (R-DX02-2, QE-R7D-P3-10), now reachable through every carrier; PREREG-3 Delta 8 retires the G03 'declare once' consumer condition that guarded it
findings.finding: A break already applied, then re-stated with a new event id and no episodeId by another event kind, is recorded, kept and applied again by the next weekly review (SAME_BREAK / DUPLICATE, revision 2). The re-entry is re-anchored and the plan ahead changes. INTERFACE-3 does not describe re-application. Whether a re-anchored re-entry is acceptable is a domain question.
findings.reproduction: probes/qe31-persistence.mjs scenario reSentAfterApplied, and probes/qe31-malformed-and-resend.mjs resend: SCHEDULE_CHANGE + break, return applied, week 5 trained, LOCAL_FATIGUE in week 6 with the same break, then a weekly review: REESTABLISH again (2 returns in total). Against a control that never re-sent it, the state traces of weeks 6 to 11 differ. Strength rows go to ESTABLISH or FROM_LOG; week 8 dumbbell rows are 22 vs 20 kg; week 9 back squat is 3x9 vs 3x11.

findings.finding: Delta 5 is labelled precision, but it is also a scoped relaxation. A complete schedule or equipment change that its own decision asked about or refused, typically because it carried a break, and that is never sent again is no longer checked by P11/P12 in the later VALID plans. On the existing corpora it removes only false FAILs. No property measures that the consumer re-sends the carrying event after the return.

HARNESS-2 P11 FAIL (18 EQUIPMENT_NOT_AVAILABLE), HARNESS-3 P11 PASS, P17 PASS (4 units).

findings.finding: P03 checks only that a declared-break row's event id and interruption match a review that sent them. A row recorded with a wrong declaredAt or a wrong athleteId at its first appearance (and any eventKind or inputHash) is not flagged by P03 or P10. Its behavioural consequence, a lost break, is caught by P17.
findings.reproduction: probes/qe31-instruments.mjs p03p10 on DEV-18: forgedRow P03 1; rewrittenFacts P03 1 + P10 REWRITTEN; rewrittenClock P10 REWRITTEN; dropped P10 DROPPED; wrongClockAtRecording 0/0; wrongAthleteAtRecording 0/0.

findings.finding: The declared break's free-text reason, often health information, is now retained in the consumer-carried record for the life of the program and replicated on every decision; before this phase it was never persisted. See answers.securityRouting.
findings.reproduction: probes/qe31-persistence.mjs scenario freeTextReason: marker in the record only (not program, decision output or reference state), on the carrier path and on the weekly-review path.

findings.finding: An early return with no new declaration (for example a later clinical flag while a break is kept) returns no actualLedger. Every client here keeps the previous record (r.actualLedger ?? previous). C3 and INTERFACE-3 say 'carry the record exactly as returned' and do not say that absent means unchanged. A literal client would lose every kept break and every execution row.
findings.reproduction: probes/qe31-persistence.mjs scenario retainedThenEarlyReturn: CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED, actualLedger absent; the carried record keeps its row only through the client's fallback.

findings.finding: Append-only holds by fact, not by position. The runtime emits declared rows after newer execution rows, so the input is not a prefix of the output at the applying review. The binding context (mode, phaseClass) of rows observed earlier in a return week is re-derived (NORMAL/BUILD to RETURN/RETURN). Identical on R7D-FREEZE-1 when the break is stated directly. P10 compares facts only.
findings.reproduction: probes/qe31-persistence.mjs appendOnly (inputIsPrefixOfOutput false at the applying review); probes/qe31-row-diff.mjs statedInWeekly on both runtimes (same context changes).

findings.finding: A carrier replayed with the same event id but other break facts is neither recorded nor refused. The first row stands and is applied, while the ASK says the break is recorded. The return handler asks event.id in the same situation. The harness client's id scheme cannot produce it.
findings.reproduction: probes/qe31-persistence.mjs replayAndCorrection.sameIdOtherFacts: rows ['2026-11-23'] only; the next weekly applies the first break (start 2026-11-23, 14 days).

- The row's inputHash is a consistency check, not authentication: a consumer-forged row with a recomputed hash is read and applied.
